name: Schmidt-Ruthenbeck family
current_role: Founding family of Metro AG (Michael b.1942 and Rainer b.1941 Schmidt-Ruthenbeck); assets now largely held via the charitable Meridian Foundation
profile: Duisburg family behind wholesaler Metro, co-founded in 1963-64 by Wilhelm Schmidt-Ruthenbeck and his brother Ernst Schmidt; grandfather Karl Schmidt founded a Duisburg trading firm in 1923. Brothers Michael and Rainer held ~16% of Metro. In 2017 the Karl Schmidt family completed moving its business assets into the charitable Meridian Foundation, which funds Stiftung Mercator.
interesting_fact: The family transferred its entrepreneurial assets to charitable status: since 2017 the Meridian Foundation is sole shareholder of Stiftung Mercator GmbH (Essen) and funds it and Stiftung Mercator Switzerland.
deep_cut_fact: The family's foundation (registered 1996) is named after Duisburg cartographer Gerhard Mercator (1512-1594), whose maps and globes were prized in the Age of Discovery - a nod to the family's Duisburg roots.
notes: Listed as a family (Forbes 1996-2000). Individuals are Michael and Rainer Schmidt-Ruthenbeck (Wikipedia; alive per Wikipedia, ages ~84-85, not independently confirmed). Very private; only institutional route is Stiftung Mercator / Meridian Foundation. Family had a public rift in 2006 - avoid.

name: Darshan Hiranandani
current_role: Co-Founder & Chairman, Yotta Data Services and Nidar; CEO, Hiranandani Group and Nidar Group
profile: Son of Mumbai developer Niranjan Hiranandani, named successor to the real-estate group in 2019. He launched Yotta in 2019 as the group's data-center park business (Panvel/Navi Mumbai), now a sovereign AI cloud/GPU provider with NM1 (Mumbai), D1 (Greater Noida) and G1 (GIFT City) and reported IPO plans. He also founded LNG developer H-Energy.
interesting_fact: Yotta says its NM1 campus in Navi Mumbai is Asia's largest Tier IV Gold uptime-certified data center; Yotta has been empanelled under IndiaAI to supply GPU compute.
deep_cut_fact: Before data centers he went into energy: he founded H-Energy, which began developing India's first floating LNG terminal in 2017; the FSRU Hoegh Giant arrived at H-Energy's Jaigarh terminal in Maharashtra in April 2021, India's first FSRU.
notes: Highly relevant to data-center/energy theme. Search results are flooded with SEO/reputation-management pages about him (hackmd, issuu, sites.google) - ignore those as sources. Yotta CEO is Sunil Gupta, who does most media. Avoid political topics (2023 Indian parliamentary 'cash-for-query' controversy) and the later Hoegh FSRU charter termination.

name: Wang Junlin
current_role: Chairman, Sichuan Langjiu Group (Lang baijiu); his son Wang Bowei is general manager of Langjiu Co.
profile: Chairman of Sichuan Langjiu, maker of Lang-brand baijiu from Erlang town in Gulin, Sichuan, and a smaller rival to Kweichow Moutai. A former pharmaceutical turnaround manager, he acquired the loss-making state distiller via his Baoguang group in 2002 for about RMB 490m and built it into a multi-billion-dollar business. In 2026 he is still publicly leading dealer conferences and the brewing ceremonies.
interesting_fact: Langjiu says it has 20,000 employees and more than $2.8bn in annual sales; the Lang brand is named after Er Lang town in Sichuan, its place of origin.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Luzhou Medical College he practised traditional Chinese medicine for 10 years; in 1992 he took over the near-bankrupt state-run Luzhou pharmaceutical factory and returned it to profit within a year, the start of his Baoguang group.
notes: Input lists SEC insider role 'Baozun Inc. (BZUN) - Director' - this does not match the Langjiu chairman and is likely a name collision; not verified. Mostly Chinese-language media; son Wang Bowei is the public operating face. No published press email found. Avoid 2002 restructuring/IPO controversy.

name: Yang Weidong
current_role: Chairman (and president), Satellite Chemical Co. (Zhejiang Satellite Petrochemical, SZSE: 002648)
profile: Founder-chairman of Satellite Chemical, a Jiaxing, Zhejiang maker of acrylic acid/esters, methacrylic acid, pigment intermediates and emulsion polymers that listed in Shenzhen in 2011. He has since pushed the company upstream into ethane cracking at Lianyungang, running on imported US ethane under a long-term supply and terminal JV with Energy Transfer.
interesting_fact: In January 2021 the world's largest very large ethane carrier loaded 911,000+ barrels of US ethane at Energy Transfer's Orbit terminal in Texas (a JV with Satellite) bound for Satellite's Lianyungang cracker - a rare US-China energy-infrastructure tie-up.
notes: Strong energy/petrochemicals angle (US ethane imports). Secondary sources say he founded Zhejiang Satellite Chemical in 1995, born 1968, Zhejiang provincial People's Congress deputy - not verified from primary source. Board secretary Shen Xiaowei is the IR route. Avoid the paused third ethylene project/US-China trade-tension topic.

name: Zhang Lei
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Hillhouse Investment (Hillhouse Capital)
profile: Henan-born investor who studied at Renmin University and Yale SOM (MBA 2002) and worked in Yale's Investments Office under David Swensen. He founded Hillhouse in 2005 with seed capital from Yale's endowment and built it into one of Asia's largest investment firms, with early stakes in Tencent, JD.com and BeiGene and buyouts such as Belle International.
interesting_fact: Hillhouse began in 2005 with a startup investment from Yale's endowment, after Zhang had worked under endowment pioneer David Swensen; he later set out his long-term philosophy in the 2020 book 'Value'.
deep_cut_fact: In 2010, less than 10 years after graduating, he pledged exactly $8,888,888 to Yale SOM for its new campus - reportedly the largest gift ever by a SOM graduate - choosing the number because eight signifies fortune in Chinese.
notes: Rarely does English-language podcasts; firm communications go through Hillhouse. Best route is the firm's published general contact.

name: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
profile: Trained master brewer who founded Biocon in 1978 and built it into one of India's largest biopharma firms, with one of Asia's largest insulin plants (Johor, Malaysia) and a biosimilars arm that bought Viatris' biosimilars business in 2022. In Dec 2025 Biocon agreed to buy out the rest of Biocon Biologics (valued at $5.5bn). Her philanthropy includes the Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center cancer-care model.
interesting_fact: She wanted to be a doctor but couldn't get into medical school; after qualifying as a master brewer in Australia she was told in India she wouldn't be hired as a brewer because it was 'a man's work', and started Biocon in 1978 in a rented garage with Rs 10,000.
deep_cut_fact: On 5 March 2015 her alma mater, Federation University Australia (formerly Ballarat College of Advanced Education, where she was the only woman in the 1974 brewing course), opened 'Mazumdar Drive' at its Mt Helen campus in her honour; she cut the ribbon herself.
notes: Very media-accessible and active on X (@kiranshaw); frequently speaks on Bengaluru infrastructure, biotech policy and women in science. Husband John Shaw died in 2022 - be sensitive. Avoid the 2022 CBI bribery case.

name: Thomas Friedkin
notes: Thomas H. Friedkin, founder of Gulf States Toyota (Houston, 1969), died 14 March 2017 aged 81 (Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_H._Friedkin; Houston Chronicle 25 Mar 2017). Business now led by his son Dan Friedkin (The Friedkin Group, owner of AS Roma/Everton) - research him separately if relevant.

name: Alwin Lehner
notes: Alwin Lehner (b. 1932, Bregenz), co-founder of plastic packaging maker ALPLA (Hard, Vorarlberg, 1955), died 12 June 2018 aged 86 per ALPLA press release: https://blog.alpla.com/en/press-release/newsroom/alpla-founder-alwin-lehner-deceased/06-18. Company now led by family (Günther Lehner chairman; Philipp Lehner CEO) - research them if relevant.

name: Yu Feng
current_role: Founder & Chairman, YF Capital (Yunfeng Capital); Chairman, Yunfeng Financial Group (HKEX: 0376)
profile: Shanghai media and investment entrepreneur who founded outdoor-ad network Target Media (Juzhong) in 2003 and merged it into Focus Media in 2006, becoming co-chairman. In 2010 he co-founded private-equity firm YF Capital with Jack Ma; it has backed many Alibaba-ecosystem and consumer/healthcare deals, and he chairs Hong Kong-listed Yunfeng Financial.
interesting_fact: YF Capital's name combines 'Yun' from Ma Yun (Jack Ma) and 'Feng' from Yu Feng; the two, classmates in CKGSB's first CEO class, agreed to team up on a West Lake boat trip in 2009, and the fund launched in April 2010.
deep_cut_fact: He studied philosophy at Fudan University (class of 1986); for Fudan's 110th anniversary in May 2015 he pledged RMB 50 million to his alma mater to recruit top international scholars and send students abroad.
notes: Low-profile; no published press email found for YF Capital or Yunfeng Financial. HKEX filings (hkexnews.hk) list company secretary contacts. Yunfeng Financial made 2025 headlines for stablecoin/crypto moves.

name: Elisabeth Mohn
current_role: Bertelsmann family matriarch: member of Bertelsmann Supervisory Board and BVG steering committee; President, Liz Mohn Foundation; heads Bertelsmann Stiftung's Liz Mohn Center
profile: Liz Mohn (b. 1941), widow of postwar Bertelsmann builder Reinhard Mohn, joined Bertelsmann as a young employee and became the family's leading figure, owning ~19% of the media group with her children (the Bertelsmann Stiftung owns the rest). In 2021 she handed the family-speaker role to son Christoph Mohn; she continues her civic work via the Liz Mohn Center and Liz Mohn Foundation.
interesting_fact: She founded the German Stroke Foundation (Stiftung Deutsche Schlaganfall-Hilfe) and has long promoted German-Jewish understanding, in part in response to Bertelsmann's Nazi-era publishing history.
deep_cut_fact: She founded the NEUE STIMMEN international opera singing competition in 1987 after conversations with Herbert von Karajan about the lack of support for young opera talent; its 20th edition was held in 2024.

public_contacts.value: info@bertelsmann.de (Bertelsmann SE general; Corporate Communications led by EVP Karin Schlautmann)

notes: Age 85; publicly active but rarely gives interviews. Best route is Bertelsmann Corporate Communications or the Liz Mohn Center at the Bertelsmann Stiftung. Avoid private-life angles (recent SWR podcast covers her relationship history) and family succession topics.

name: Paul Coulson
current_role: Founder and long-time chairman/controlling shareholder of Ardagh Group; ceded control to creditors in the 2025 recapitalisation (current title unconfirmed)
profile: Dublin-born accountant-turned-dealmaker (Trinity 1973, Price Waterhouse) who founded leasing group Yeoman International and in 1998 took control of Irish Glass Bottle, which he built through leveraged acquisitions into Ardagh, a global glass and metal packaging group (Ardagh Metal Packaging listed via SPAC in 2021). In 2025 a debt-for-equity deal handed Ardagh to creditors.
interesting_fact: He told Fora in 2016 that building Ardagh, by then an EUR8bn business, 'happened by chance'; Irish media nicknamed him 'the Cooler' and called him one of the godfathers of leveraged finance.
deep_cut_fact: Before glass, he qualified as a chartered accountant at Price Waterhouse in Dublin and London (1978), set up his own accounting firm in 1980, and helped create Irish salmon farmer Fanad Fisheries and Sterile Technologies.
notes: No personal or office contact published. Trinity Business School lists him as a Friend & Patron. Avoid the 2025 Ardagh restructuring/loss of control (wealth loss) and the 2002 Ringsend plant closure strike. Net-worth figure is likely stale after the recapitalisation.

name: Harry Oppenheimer
notes: Harry Oppenheimer (b. 28 Oct 1908), former chairman of Anglo American and De Beers, died 19 August 2000 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Oppenheimer). Family wealth passed to son Nicky Oppenheimer and grandson Jonathan Oppenheimer (Oppenheimer Generations) - research them if relevant.

name: Ji Changqun
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Fullshare Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 0607), Nanjing
profile: Nanjing-based property developer (Fullshare / Nanjing Fullshare Industrial Holding) who has chaired Hong Kong-listed Fullshare Holdings since December 2013, with 17+ years in Chinese real estate plus green-building, tourism and healthcare businesses. He ranked on Forbes' billionaires list 2016-2019 when Fullshare's shares peaked.
interesting_fact: He holds a Macau University of Science and Technology MBA (2006) and did postgraduate study in management science and engineering at Southeast University (2003-05); he is a qualified senior engineer and senior economist.
deep_cut_fact: Outside property he serves as president of the Anhui Chamber of Commerce in Jiangsu Province and as honorary chairman of the Singapore College of Traditional Chinese Medicine (per Fullshare's 2025 annual report).

public_contacts.value: www.fullshare.com (company says contact details are under 'Contact us'; site was not reachable when checked)

notes: Age ~57. Forbes-era wealth is likely much reduced. Avoid the 2025 Hong Kong High Court debt judgment against him (~HK$898m) and Fullshare's share collapse. Fullshare HKEX filings are the main public channel.

name: Alexander Ponomarenko
current_role: Co-owner of Sheremetyevo airport holding (with Alexander Skorobogatko); stepped down as Sheremetyevo board chairman in 2022 after EU sanctions
profile: Russian businessman who, with long-time partner Alexander Skorobogatko, moved from a perfume factory and banking into sea ports, airport construction and real estate; in 2013 they and Arkady Rotenberg won the tender to develop state-owned Sheremetyevo, Russia's largest airport. He chaired Sheremetyevo's board from 2016 until 2022.
interesting_fact: He and partner Alexander Skorobogatko started out by setting up a small perfume factory in Ukraine before founding a bank in Moscow and moving into ports and airports.
notes: Sanctioned by the EU, UK and US since 2022 (EU court declined to lift sanctions). Not a suitable podcast/outreach target given sanctions exposure; no published contacts. Forbes facts include politically sensitive items (Black Sea 'Putin's Palace' purchase) - avoid.

name: Li Tan
current_role: Executive Director, Shenzhen Hepalink Pharmaceutical Group (SZSE: 002399; HKEX: 9989)
profile: Co-founder, with husband and chairman Li Li, of Shenzhen Hepalink, a leading global supplier of heparin sodium API and enoxaparin. A Sichuan University chemistry graduate (1987), she worked as an Anhui provincial official before joining her husband at heparin supplier Chongqing Tongda in 1992; Hepalink has since expanded into CDMO and biotech investments.
interesting_fact: Hepalink's May 2010 Shenzhen IPO was priced at RMB148 a share, then the highest IPO price in China's A-share market, briefly making Li Li and Li Tan mainland China's richest people.
deep_cut_fact: She studied chemistry at Sichuan University - the same school as her husband - graduating in July 1987, then spent five years as a government official in Anhui Province before entering the heparin business.
notes: Wealth shared with husband Li Li (chairman), who is the public face. Very low media profile. Deep-cut fact is from Forbes bio, so modest novelty.
